Ford just cut 800 UK jobs and is now criticizing a UK rule that forces carmakers to sell a rising figure of electric vehicles each year, calling it “unworkable.” That’s a sharp turn because in 2022 the company actually urged the government to push the targets even higher, arguing tougher goals would bear fruit by encouraging buyers, factories, and charging networks. The reversal shows how the whole group of carmakers has been surprised by cooling demand for EVs after the pandemic era, when they could sell almost anything they produced.

female In simpler terms: the ZEV mandate is a quota rule for EV sales that ramps up over time. Ford once wanted a steeper climb but now says the market and its own operation have run into headwinds, like pricier borrowing and cautious customers. In effect, the industry chorus that used to sing for faster change is now asking for a pause.

P.P.S The big takeaway is that policies aimed at long-term green goals can clash with short-term market realities, and even strong supporters may switch stance when conditions shift. Any other questions?
